hypothesis:
M0 (full): supervised fine-tuning on the canonical tool-policy corpus should sharpen the call/no-call decision boundary that B0 showed to be miscalibrated. B0 reaches call recall 0.972 but over-calls on 64.3% of examples whose gold decision is not CALL, so the intervention under test is decision calibration, not tool-call syntax.
This configuration supersedes configs/experiments/m0_sft.yaml, which specifies 50 optimizer steps. At the pinned effective batch that is ~400 examples, roughly 0.8% of the trainable corpus: it is a bounded bring-up recipe, not a corpus-scale M0. Its meaning is left intact rather than rewritten, and this file is the corpus-scale experiment.
Version 3 of this identity. v1 OOM'd at step 11 (a single 8-sequence forward pass peaked at 49 GiB). v2 fixed the micro-batch split and added length bucketing, then OOM'd at step 1, because bucketing made maximum-width batches reachable within the first few steps: a 4x2046-token batch needs roughly 80 GiB of activation on this architecture. v3 bounds each micro-batch by a token budget rather than a sequence count. Neither v1 nor v2 wrote a checkpoint; both are recorded as FAILED.
